newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to seek $2.1 mln to improve CPI - Labor Dept.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to seek $2.1 mln to improve CPI - Labor Dept.

text.p: A request for $2.1 million to accelerate improvements to the Consumer Price Index will be included in President Clinton's budget for fiscal year 1998, the Labor Department said Thursday.

"This proposal, coupled with the major ongoing multi-year revision of the CPI, will assure the American people that we have the most accurate data possible," Acting Labor Secretary Cynthia Metzler said in a statement.
The White House is scheduled to unveil its 1998 budget proposal on February 6.
The additional money would go toward the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics, which publishes the CPI.
Earlier on Thursday, BLS Commissioner Katharine Abraham told the Senate Budget Committee that more money would be requested to improve the CPI, but she provided no dollar figure.

Abraham said the additional money would allow the BLS to improve methods used to adjust the CPI for "quality change" by expanding the amount of information collected on the prices and characteristics of certain goods and services.
Some of the money would also be used to speed up the updating of the CPI market basket in future revisions.
Additionally, some funds would go toward looking at potential alternative cost-of-living measures.
